text.en: A mule is stronger and more resistant to disease than its horse and donkey parents, but it is sterile. Why do breeders cross different breeds?

Animal breeding improves milk, egg, meat and wool production and resistance to disease.
Inbreeding is mating of animals of the same breed and keeps pure lines, but continued inbreeding reduces vigour.
Outbreeding crosses different breeds and gives hybrids with heterosis.
The mule, a cross of a male donkey and a female horse, is stronger and more intelligent than a horse but is sterile.
Hissardale is a sheep breed developed in Punjab from Australian Merino rams and Bikaneri ewes.
Karan Swiss is a cattle breed developed at NDRI, Karnal from Brown Swiss and Sahiwal cattle for high milk yield.
Breeding aims at higher milk by cattle, more eggs from poultry, high quality meat and faster growth in domesticated animals.

problem.en: Why is a mule sterile although it is a vigorous hybrid?

text.en: A mule comes from a horse and a donkey, two different species.
Its chromosomes cannot pair properly in meiosis.
Hence heterosis gives vigour but the mule is sterile.

requiredIdeas.en: Inbreeding: same breed, pure line, risk of reduced vigour

points.en: Inbreeding: same breed; outbreeding: different breeds.
Hissardale and Karan Swiss are improved breeds.
